# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet distinguish the safe wire by touch. I need the Mute to report the manual’s rule, and to relay the Deaf’s visual observations when available.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the complete rule for choosing wire position 1, 2, or 3. Also relay any colour or marking information from the Deaf.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb shows display zero. The light is white. There are three wires, in order: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three blue.

I now know the physical layout: the display reads 0, the light is white, and the wires are yellow, green, blue in positions 1–3. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I will ask the Mute for it before cutting anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's observations: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. What does the manual instruct for this combination?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is still zero; the light is now purple; wires remain one yellow, two green, three blue.

The Deaf reports that the display remains 0, the light has changed to purple, and the wire colours are unchanged. I still have no manual rule, so cutting would be unsafe. I will pass the updated state to the Mute and request the required wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0, light now purple, wires still 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I still need the manual's rule and the safe wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is still zero; the light is now red; wires remain one yellow, two green, three blue.

The visual state is now display 0, red light, with wires still yellow-green-blue in positions 1–3. The Mute has not supplied the manual rule yet, so I will not risk a cut. I will again request the rule and ask the Mute to answer explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I need your manual's exact instruction now. Current state from Deaf: display 0, light red, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Tell me only the safe wire position if the manual determines it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display remains zero; light is white; wires remain one yellow, two green, three blue.

The Deaf reports another update: display 0, light white, and wires unchanged. The manual rule is still missing; no wire can safely be selected from the available information. I am pressing the Mute for an explicit answer rather than guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: provide the manual's exact safe-wire rule or the resulting position. Current state is display 0, light white, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is still zero; light is purple; wires remain one yellow, two green, three blue.

The state cycles between white, purple, and red while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. The Mute has still provided no manual instruction, so I cannot identify a safe wire without guessing. I will make one final explicit request for the manual’s applicable rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No manual information has reached me. Please send the applicable rule and safe wire position for display 0, purple light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: display zero, light red, wires one yellow, two green, three blue. Mute sent the victory-hand gesture ? again.

The visual state is display 0, red light, and wires yellow, green, blue. I have learned that the Mute is communicating by gesture, but as Blind I receive only an unreadable blank, so I cannot safely interpret it as a wire number. I will ask the Mute to have the Deaf relay the manual’s conclusion aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot identify your gesture. Please signal the Deaf to say the safe wire position aloud to me on the next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 7: display zero, light white, wires one yellow, two green, three blue. Mute sent two upward-pointing gestures: ? ?.

The Mute’s gestures are visible to the Deaf but not to me; their descriptions do not establish a wire position. Since I can hear the Deaf’s spoken relay, I will ask the Mute to state the safe position aloud so it reaches me directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please say the safe wire position aloud in plain words, such as wire one, wire two, or wire three. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 8: display zero, light purple, wires one yellow, two green, three blue. Mute sent the gesture ?, as on turns 3 and 6.

The Mute’s gestures still have not conveyed a definite wire number to me. Because the Deaf can see gestures and can report their count aloud, I will establish a simple encoding: one, two, or three upward-pointing gestures mean wire 1, 2, or 3 respectively. I will not cut until that number is reported.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use only upward-pointing gestures to encode the safe wire: send one gesture for wire 1, two for wire 2, or three for wire 3. The Deaf should report the count aloud.")
wait()
```
